description: Binding compatibility policy for API clients, rolling backend deployments, PostgreSQL schema phases, persisted jobs/Previews, parser artifacts and object versions. A pinned dependency or same-version test does not prove mixed-version compatibility.

compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: URL major plus machine-readable request/response contracts
compatibleChanges: add optional response fields that clients must ignore when unknown
add a new endpoint or optional capability without changing existing semantics
add a new closed-enum value only after older clients have an explicit unknown-value behavior
tighten server-side internal implementation without changing public status/error semantics
breakingChanges: remove or rename a request or response field
change field meaning, units, authority or nullability
change an existing success or error condition incompatibly
make an optional request field required
reuse an enum token with new meaning
move an existing v1 route without a compatibility bridge

compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: canonical migration sequence and application source SHA
compatibleChanges: expand schema before application dependence
keep old and new application access paths during the mixed-version window
run bounded idempotent backfills separately
contract only after old-version drain and verification
breakingChanges: deploy new code before required expansion exists
drop a surface still used by a deployable old version
change RLS or authority semantics without old/new negative tests
couple destructive contraction to the same release that introduces the replacement

compatibilityDimensions.consumer: old backend instance and shared dependencies
compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: source commit SHA and deployment generation
compatibleChanges: both versions operate against the expanded schema
both versions preserve the same tenant, idempotency and object-binding invariants
new writes remain readable or safely ignorable by the old version during the observation window
breakingChanges: new persisted state crashes or is misinterpreted by the old version
old workers consume a new job/spool format without version gating
one version weakens a security or deletion invariant
rollback target cannot start against the expanded schema

compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: explicit schema/adapter/options/artifact/source version bindings and hashes
compatibleChanges: read a known older version through a tested adapter
introduce a new version without reinterpreting existing bytes
fail closed on unknown or conflicting version/hash bindings
preserve exact Preview and object version identity across retries
breakingChanges: reinterpret existing persisted bytes under a new implicit schema
accept unknown versions as latest
change canonical record meaning in place
drop a version reader while persisted work can still reference it

compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: adapter id, adapter version and artifact SHA-256
compatibleChanges: new artifact under a new reviewed digest with unchanged declared output contract
explicit adapter-version upgrade with fixture and canonical-record verification
continued availability of an older artifact while persisted work remains bound to it
breakingChanges: replace bytes behind an existing digest/version claim
allow operator-supplied unreviewed digest in production
change canonical output meaning without a version change
delete an artifact required for retry/reconciliation before retention review

compatibilityDimensions.producer: signed upload client and object store
compatibilityDimensions.versionSignal: bucket, object key, exact object version id, length, checksum and metadata
compatibleChanges: read the exact bound object version
retain older versions according to reviewed lifecycle requirements
reject latest-version substitution or metadata drift
breakingChanges: read an unbound latest version
expire a version still referenced by a job, Preview, retry or incident record
change object metadata authority or checksum semantics

compatibilityMatrix.oldComponent: current PostgreSQL schema before required expansion

releaseGates: record exact old and new source/deployment/schema versions
classify every changed public or persisted contract as compatible or breaking
run old/new mixed-version tests for changed shared state
prove rollback target starts and preserves security/deletion invariants
verify unknown version and enum behavior fails closed or is explicitly ignored as designed
keep schema contraction separate until old-version drain
retain required parser artifacts and object versions for in-flight and retry windows
update the compatibility matrix and evidence references before rollout
block release when a required direction is NOT_PROVEN or FORBIDDEN

readiness.note: Compatibility directions and release gates are explicit. Only the current backend against a clean current PostgreSQL 16 schema is proven in the canonical release matrix. Candidate-only, local-CI-only and empty-registry foundations are recorded separately and cannot promote release compatibility; OPS-P0-008 stays PARTIAL.
